title: Seasonal changes in fish production in annual and perennial eelgrass (Zostera marina) beds of the western North Pacific
content:
Abstract

Eelgrass (Zostera marina) beds form essential ecosystems that provide significant ecosystem services through carbon fixation and as nurseries for aquatic living resources. The period during which vegetation is in decline or has disappeared in annual eelgrass beds is longer than in perennial eelgrass beds. There have been no comparative studies of fish production in eelgrass beds with the different life cycles, although quantitative evaluation of fish production within habitats is an essential process for assessing the contribution of each habitat to fisheries resources. We conducted field surveys at two eelgrass beds (annual eelgrass in 2023–2024 and perennial eelgrass in 2008–2009) in temperate coastal waters of the western North Pacific to evaluate how the difference in eelgrass life cycle affects seasonal change and annual amount of fish production. Fish production was estimated by monthly seines that enabled species-specific estimates of biomass increase. The results showed that monthly fish production in the perennial eelgrass bed remained at higher levels for a longer period than in the annual eelgrass bed, and annual fish production in the perennial eelgrass bed was approximately twice that in the annual eelgrass bed. Because the increase in sea water temperature and changes in other environmental conditions under global warming are expected to shift eelgrass towards an annual life cycle, this could affect ecosystem services of eelgrass bed through changes in fish community structure and production.
